As a venerable Elvaland, you have been appointed by the King. Search through every tavern in the kingdom, hire the most skillful dwarves, recruit the most prestigious heroes, and build the best battalion you can to defeat your mortal enemy! Each turn in Nidavellir, bid a coin on each tavern. In descending order, choose a character and add this character to your army. Each dwarf class has its own scoring way: blacksmith, hunter, warrior, explorer, and miner. A meticulous recruitment will allow you to attract a powerful hero to your army. You will also be able to increase the value of your gold coins thanks to the smart 'coin-building' system, and get the best of the other Elvalands. Resolve each tavern one by one: Turn over only the coins assigned to the tavern currently being resolved. Bid Revelation: The tokens placed by each player to the current tavern is revealed automatically. Choose a card: The active player takes a Dwarf or Royal Offering card. Recruit a Hero: If active player just filled up a new row, they can take a hero card. Replace coins: If active player played 0 , add up the values of the 2 coins in your pouch, and replace the bigger with the coin showing the sum. Royal Offering: Add the offering value to any one of your non-zero coins - including one assigned to a tavern that has not yet been resolved - and replace that coin with one of the resulting value from the Royal Treasure chest. If the replaced coin originally came from the chest, put it back there, otherwise return it to the game box. If you change the coin that you assigned to the current tavern, the original coin value still applies when deciding whether and how to swap jewels. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] I ordered a French version of this game but the rules are written with a strange post-modern version of my language that I absolutely refuse to read.  So I had to send the game back and I told the website that they SHOULD HAVE explained in their description of the game that the rules were written in this horrible fashion that defiles my mother tongue.

[Rating: 1/10] An auction game combined with set collection.  Nidaevllir isn't terrible but Knizia dominates this space -> 45 minutes -> play 3  games of High Society or Modern Art which both produce laughs. + Art is nice and the upgrading of bidding tokens is interesting – Blind bidding, a lot of the time you don't have any feeling for your opposition wants and sometimes the 3 card offer is so similar you don't care – Too long, played on BGA it took 16 minutes, this would be 45 in real life heh I'm heading to the tavern for an ale right now!   – Sets feel similar, Sushi Go sets are simpler and better – Scor

[Rating: 1/10] There's hardly any tension over the bidding, so I guess it's just a set collecting game. And it doesn't do much with that, so it's over. The end!  Why are the coin boards shaped like a phallus?

[Rating: 2/10] The amount of components, setup and special widgets (probably the fault of the expansion) is completely out of alignment with the game being a simple blind bidding auction for set collection scoring. Upgrading your bidding currency is the single interesting decision the game offers.

[Rating: 2/10] boring, themeless game that has a cool auction mechanic but the game can be almost lost on turn 1.  The simplicity is good but ultimately it's just a min-max filler game

[Rating: 2/10] Imbalanced/skewed game play is baked into the design of this game and there is no catch-up mechanism. One unhappy face at the table guaranteed. In addition, the iconography is particularly poor in this game.

[Rating: 2/10] Sorry but its boring and repeating...in some game i was just do the bidding complete random without looking at them....still manage to get high score.

[Rating: 3/10] I know I'm in the minority, but this game was not fun at all. The rulebook was horrible, too.

[Rating: 3/10] UPDATE: JUNE 2022  :star::star::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Yup. Downgrade to 2 stars  ===============================  Good auction game, but I feel like it doesn't stand to the greatness of Knizia's auction games or The Estates or other top-of-the-line auction titles.  I might downgrade it to 2 stars if the game starts to become more obvious (despite the blind auction, some rounds are bit obvious)
